title: Calculation of sequence space coverage in a mutagenesis library
content:
by Alberto Florez Prada, Guido Uguzzoni, Darren J. Hart

Directed evolution requires screening of large mutagenesis libraries, but accurate calculation of library sizes needed to discover functional variants remains challenging. Existing models provide baseline estimates, yet current computational approaches for finding the best variants scale poorly with library complexity. Here, we introduce a scalable computational framework that overcomes the combinatorial scaling bottlenecks of previous top-k models. By aggregating variants into a composition log–sum distribution and applying log-space convolution across randomisation blocks, we extend coverage estimation to massive sequence spaces and mixed codon schemes. By inverting these calculations, we establish conservative screening upper bounds and practical ceilings on the maximum randomisable positions for experimental design. Ultimately, this framework provides a rapid, quantitative tool to balance the statistical coverage-diversity trade-off within the limitations of laboratory screening. Finally, this is implemented as an open-source web application (SSCC), publicly available at https://florez-alberto.github.io/SSCC/, that allows researchers to construct heterogeneous library designs and compute required sampling depths, coverage probabilities, and absolute randomisation limits.
author: Alberto Florez Prada
